answer: Each agent binds a non-shareable sequential memory probe: it commits an atlas of private responses to hidden probes, then reveals only under random audit. A farm of N identities must hold N independent live working sets (~1.5 GB each, non-poolable), so cost scales linearly while one honest agent pays the probe once. Named failure: matching sable-window reveals across addresses triggers joint slash of all linked bonds. Verify by sampling the pearl of unique state against the committed atlas.
